questions.question: For LT11 or Letter 1058, what does the IRS say to do if I cannot pay the full overdue balance?

response.answer: IRS guidance says: If you can’t pay the full amount, pay what you can now; payments will reduce the amount of interest and applicable penalties added to the remaining balance in the future. IRS guidance says: If you’re current on your tax filings, you can request an [installment agreement](https://www.irs.gov/payments/payment-plans-installment-agreements) to pay the remaining balance on your account over time. IRS guidance says: If you owe less than $50,000, you may be able to set up an installment agreement using the [Online Payment Agreement tool](https://www.irs.gov/payments/online-payment-agreement-application), which is the fastest way to get an installment agreement approved. IRS guidance says: If you can’t apply online, call us at the number on your notice or letter, or mail in an [installment agreement request PDF](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f9465--dft.pdf). IRS guidance says: If you’re unable to pay the balance due, contact the telephone number listed on the notice or letter.

questions.question: The IRS says it still hasn't heard from me and calls this my second reminder about an unpaid balance. What stage is this, and what could happen if I keep ignoring it?

response.answer: IRS guidance says: This notice is your second reminder that you still owe a balance on one of your tax accounts. You received this notice because we haven’t received your payment or a response to previous notice(s) requesting you pay this balance. IRS guidance says: If you don't pay the amount due, make payment arrangements, or contact us at the toll-free number on your notice, we may file a Notice of Federal Tax Lien if we haven't already done so. A tax lien is a public notice to your creditors that the IRS has a right to your interests in your current assets and any assets you acquire after we file the lien; it can affect your ability to get credit.

questions.question: I have CP523 and disagree with the reason for ending my installment agreement. What can I do, and what should I do if I already corrected the problem?

response.answer: IRS guidance says: If you don't agree with our reason for terminating your installment agreement, contact us at the number printed at the top of the notice. IRS guidance says: If you have already taken corrective action, you should still call us to make sure we have a record of your action so that we can reinstate your installment agreement. IRS guidance says: You may have to pay a fee to reinstate it or you may have to pay any new tax liability in full. IRS guidance says: If you don't respond, we will terminate your installment agreement and begin taking collection action, which can include filing a federal tax lien or seizing (levying) your wages and/or bank accounts. IRS guidance says: If after talking with us you still do not agree, you have the right to file an appeal and can request a hearing with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals.

Understanding your CP59 notice

Notice: CP59

Section:
Frequently asked questions > What can happen if I don’t file? (added April 17, 2025)

If you don’t file, you may lose your claim to a refund or certain credits because the Internal Revenue Code sets [strict time limits](https://www.irs.gov/filing/time-you-can-claim-a-credit-or-refund) to claim those items. If you owe money, penalties and interest will continue to accrue until you file and pay in full.

questions.question: I have CP523 and disagree with the reason for ending my installment agreement. What can I do, and what should I do if I already corrected the problem?

response.answer: IRS guidance says: If you don't agree with our reason for terminating your installment agreement, contact us at the number printed at the top of the notice. If after talking with us you still do not agree, you have the right to file an appeal and can request a hearing with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals. IRS guidance says: If you have already taken corrective action, you should still call us to make sure we have a record of your action so that we can reinstate your installment agreement.

heading_path: What if I don't agree with your action or have already taken corrective action?
cited_evidence.text:
Understanding your CP523 notice

Notice: CP523

Section:
Frequently asked questions > What if I don't agree with your action or have already taken corrective action?

If you don't agree with our reason for terminating your installment agreement, contact us at the number printed at the top of the notice. If after talking with us you still do not agree, you have the right to file an appeal and can request a hearing with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals.

If you have already taken corrective action, you should still call us to make sure we have a record of your action so that we can reinstate your installment agreement.
